topics.title: moab33's Math Tips #4: Sum of Divisors
topics.text:
Welcome back for moab33's Math Tips #$3!-2=4$.



Well, let's look at $12$. Hm. Why not sum the  proper divisors of it? $1+2+4+6$. Hey, that's more than $12$! If $f(x)$ is the sum of divisors of $x$, and $f(x)>x$, $x$ is called abundant.



Now, let's look at $16$. Oh, that's just $1+2+4+8$, or $15$. Wait! Now $f(x)<x$! So, we call $x$ deficient. (It must not be eating enough!)



Now, how about $28$. Let's see... $1+2+4+7+14$. Oh no! That's $28$! What do we call this? We call it perfect. So, $f(x)=x$.



Note that the real mathematical Sum-of-Divisors function is $\sigma(x)$. So,

If $\sigma(x)>x$, then $x$ is called abundant.

If $\sigma(x)<x$, then $x$ is called deficient.

If $\sigma(x)=x$, then $x$ is called  perfect.

Also, there is one more that I looked at:

If $\sigma(x)=x-1$, then $x$ is called almost perfect.



Thanks for reading this!



~moab33

topics.title: PSA: Learn what modulo is. It makes algebra/num theory easie
topics.text:
Brief preview. Don't be put off by the weird notation. Modulo is simply the remainder function.  In 25≡1 mod 6, 6 is the divisor, 25 is the dividend and 1 is the remainder. (How ever b isn't always the remainder) Using the above example, a more concrete definition would be, given a≡b mod n, a-b is divisible by n.

Here are some links:



Start off with this reddit explainlikeim5: https://www.reddit.com/r/explainlikeimfive/comments/1xws9k/eli5_modulo/cffanex



If you want to read a more advanced explanation: http://www.math.cornell.edu/~morris/135/mod.pdf



Rules/Theorems (try to prove them on your own so it becomes easier to remember): http://math.stackexchange.com/q/346277



Modulo is a little hard to learn because it is never mentioned in grade school math as far as I know.

topics.title: 2012 AIME I Problem 3 Solution 2
topics.text:
So I was reading the solution by MathleteMA, but I have no idea how he got to 3!. I think I'm just missing something, but could someone please care to explain the 3! part? Thanks! :)





Nine people sit down for dinner where there are three choices of meals. Three people order the beef meal, three order the chicken meal, and three order the fish meal. The waiter serves the nine meals in random order. Find the number of ways in which the waiter could serve the meal types to the nine people so that exactly one person receives the type of meal ordered by that person.

____________________________________________________________________________________________________

Since there are three people who want each type of meal there are $3!=6$ ways the waiter can serve one type of dish. For the waiter to serve all the dishes, there are $6\times 6 \times 6 = \boxed{216}$ total ways to serve all the corresponding dishes to the corresponding people.



~MathleteMA

topics.title: Mathfights Question Thread
topics.text:
MATHFIGHTS QUESTION THREAD

[quote="Tiks"]

P.S. One little request guys: this thread has gotten really long so most AoPSers don't know the full picture anymore and still think that mathfights is invite only (I keep on getting invite requests :) ), so if you have any spin off topics to discuss regarding mathfights, feel free to kick off a separate discussions and just put a mathfights tag on them so that I can keep tabs and reply as needed.[/quote]

This is the question thread, for all of your questions regarding the site Mathfights.

If you haven't seen the site before, go check it out, and if you like it, sign up!

This is the Mathfights Questions thread! You can ask any questions you have.

Tiks, the founder of Mathfights, will respond to your questions.





FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS



Is Mathfights free to use?

Yes, Mathfights is free, and will always be free!



What does the "x fights left" mean at the top of the main screen? How does the progress bar work?

On the progress bar, there is a Relegation line and a Promotion line. The "x fights left" mean how many fights you have left to try to get past the Promotion bar. If after your fights run out, and the bar is not at the Relegation line yet, then you are demoted a rank. If it is in between the Relegation and the Promotion lines, you stay in the same rank and restart the bar and your fights left (confirm?). If after you run out of fights and the bar is over the Promotion line, then you get promoted a rank. Every time to start a new rank, you start with 10 fights.



How are the amount of coins you get calculated?

The amount of coins you get is directly proportional to the score you get in a game. Rank may also have a factor with this.



Are the opponents bots?

Don't worry, your opponents are not bots! They are real people, just like you.



Can you challenge your friends? Will there be groups you can join?

You can challenge your friends! Click the "Challenge a Friend" button on the left, and then send the link to a friend. When they join, you can play them! However, there are no groups to join yet.



How does the performance graph work?

The performance graph plots if you had won or lost or tied (green, red, and yellow dot respectively). It also plots how much you won or how much you lost. (Exact algorithm not known by me)



Is there a Mathfights forum?

Not yet, but it is planned. Stay tuned!



Can we have our own avatars? Can we customize our avatars?

Unfortunately, you cannot have your own avatars as it would mess up the theme of the website. However, bronze, silver, and gold versions of the current avatars are planned to be implemented, and you can also ask Tiks to make a custom tailored avatar available if you have a good enough idea.



Can we change the time of a round or the number of questions of a round?

Sorry, but that probably won't happen any time soon. [quote="Tiks"]We are thinking of changing the number of rounds but we also think that the current system has it's advantages. First it encourages to double check your work not to make a mistake and second it keeps the fights short and quick so you won't get too tired.[/quote]



Where can you suggest changes or additions to Mathfights?

You can use the "Send Feedback" button on the left side, or post your suggestion on the main Mathfights Thread. However, not all suggestions on the Mathfights thread might be read, as Tiks might miss a suggestion.



Will there be a chat area?

Probably. It is on the list of planned additions to the game.



Will there be powerups?

It's an interesting idea, although Tiks needs to see if there is enough support for it. So if you want this, shoot him a message on the "Send Feedback" button!



Can we send problems to Mathfights to use? Will there be special prizes for doing so?

This seems like a really good idea, and it might be implemented. There might be a badge for sending a good question, a special "Contributor" status, or having your name highlighted in a different color!



How many people are there on Mathfights?

As of 10/6/2013, there are close to 16,800 players in all. However, the number keeps growing.



How do I signup?

If you enter the Mathfights landing page, there is a "sign-up" button you can click in the top right corner. Some personal information is required, but don't worry. Mathfights is completely safe.



What happens if you get promoted from Division 1?

Right now, there is nothing after Division 1. If you do get to Division 1 and reach promotion, congratulations! Unfortunately, your page will not be able to load and you'll have to contact an admin to fix that.



Is there something wrong with the timing? 

No, the timing is set up like that. It may seem like you start at around 2:45 or something, but your opponent has that too. You may have also noticed that near the end, things get weird. That is also normal.



How much money do you get in each division?

As a general rule, the higher division you are, the more money you get. In divisions under 5, you can get a few hundred per round. Closer to 1, you can get up to 3000 per round.

Let $f(x) = x^4 + x^3$. Find the remainder when $f(x)$ is divided by $x^2 - 1$.



$f(x) = (x^2 - 1)q(x) + r$ for some $q(x)$. If $x = 1$, then $f(x) = f(1) = 0\cdot q(x) + r = 2$. However, if $x = -1$, then $f(-1) = 0 \cdot q(x) + r = 0$.



Am I doing something wrong here?

topics.title: MATHCOUNTS State Sprint 2009 Problem 22
topics.text:
The arithmetic progressions {2, 5, 8, 11, ...} and {3, 10, 17, 24, ...} have some common values.  What is the largest value less than 500 that they have in common?



Slightly Bashy SolutionIt is obvious that the first sequence is 2 mod 3 and the second is 3 mod 7.  Thus, we start from 500 and move down listing all numbers that are 2 mod 3 or 3 mod 7 and it doesn't take long to get that the ans is 479.




Is there a more elegant way to do this, say if the problem came up on the AMCs and it wasn't as easily bashable?
